transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

A fridge temperature of 10°C while the freezer remains frozen usually points to an airflow issue rather than a complete loss of cooling. In most integrated frost-free models, cold air is generated in the freezer and blown into the fridge via a vent or fan. The two most likely causes are:
1. Blocked Airflow: Ice may have built up behind the freezer’s back panel (often triggered by a failed defrost heater or drain), blocking the vent that sends cold air to the fridge.
2. Fan Failure: The evaporator fan inside the freezer might have stopped, so the freezer stays cold but no air reaches the fridge compartment. Please check if there is visible ice at the back of the freezer and listen for a faint humming sound from inside the freezer area when it’s running.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
There's some frost on the back of the freezer, not loads. I can hear it running a lot but can't tell if that's a fan. No burning smell and nothing tripping.

The 'some frost' you see suggests the automatic defrost cycle may not be clearing ice properly. If the evaporator fan is running (which the noise might be), but cold air isn't reaching the fridge because of a blockage or a failed heater/thermostat, that explains why the freezer stays cold but the fridge warms up. To identify the specific component to check or replace, I need the make and model number. This is usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment (often near the salad drawer or on the side wall). Can you read that for me?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Found the label inside the fridge: it's a Hotpoint HMCB 7030 AA.

Thanks for getting that model number. With the Hotpoint HMCB 7030 AA showing 'some frost' and the fridge at 10°C while the freezer is fine, this strongly points to a defrost system failure—likely the heater or thermostat has stopped working, causing ice to build up behind the panel and block airflow. Since you are in a rented flat and cannot dismantle the appliance, the best next step is a manual defrost. Please switch it off at the socket and leave both doors open for 24 hours (use towels for any water). Once dry, plug it back in and set the temperatures to fridge +4°C and freezer -18°C. As this requires replacing internal components behind the panels, I would recommend contacting your landlord or letting them know it needs an engineer.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

candidates: Airflow blockage or fan fault (cold air not reaching fridge) (high)
Defrost system failure (ice blocking vents behind freezer panel) (medium)
